record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Is there a higher-dimensional analogue of boundary-conformal-field-theory approaches to diagnosing and characterizing topological phases of matter, especially in settings where the relevant surface theories of (3+1)-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases may be gapless or may carry topological order?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to explore if there is a higher dimensional analogue of the approaches discussed in this article.

artifact.category_tag: Boundary conformal field theory and SPT phases
artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase in (d+1) spacetime dimensions is a gapped quantum phase of matter with a global symmetry G whose ground state is short-range entangled and which becomes trivial once the symmetry G is broken explicitly. A characteristic feature is that the boundary of an SPT cannot be simultaneously gapped, symmetric, and non-degenerate: the surface theory must either spontaneously break G, be gapless, or carry intrinsic topological order. Boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) provides a framework for studying quantum field theories on manifolds with boundary by specifying conformal boundary conditions; in (1+1)-dimensional bulk/boundary settings, BCFT methods (boundary states, g-functions, boundary RG flows, etc.) have been used to diagnose and characterize (2+1)-dimensional SPT phases via their (1+1)-dimensional anomalous edge theories.

Problem: Develop a higher-dimensional analogue of these BCFT-based methods for diagnosing and characterizing topological phases of matter. Specifically, formulate BCFT techniques applicable to (3+1)-dimensional SPT phases protected by a symmetry G whose (2+1)-dimensional boundary theories may be either gapless conformal field theories or carry intrinsic topological order. Identify boundary observables (analogous to boundary entropies, anomaly inflow data, or boundary partition functions on appropriate backgrounds) defined on conformal boundaries of four-dimensional CFTs that:
(i) detect the 't Hooft anomaly of G on the (2+1)-dimensional surface,
(ii) distinguish inequivalent (3+1)-dimensional SPT phases protected by G, and
(iii) constrain renormalization-group flows between admissible surface theories (gapless or topologically ordered) that saturate the same bulk anomaly.
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for a higher-dimensional analogue of BCFT diagnostics for SPT phases, including (3+1)D SPTs with gapless or topologically ordered surfaces. This is a broadly framed research direction rather than a precise conjecture; no comprehensive solution appears in the literature, and related programs (symmetry TFT/SymTFT, anomaly inflow, higher-dimensional BCFT) are still active areas of investigation. The status is best described as open.
